findings.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup hook registered inside the creation loop removes the identity provider with alias "alias", which is never created by this test — the created providers are all named "idp-alias-<i>", so this is a copy-paste from testCacheIDPByOrg and no created provider is ever cleaned up. At cleanup, testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias").remove() issues a DELETE for a nonexistent IDP and fails (404/NotFoundException) instead of removing the 20 created "idp-alias-N" providers, so the test leaks IDPs into the realm and pollutes subsequent test runs; the same wrong "alias" cleanup is repeated again at the idp-alias-20 creation site (~line 412), compounding the leak. Test isolation breaks and the cleanup itself can fail the test run.

[BUG] getForLogin applies createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel on the isInvalid path and the getById-null fallback path, but the primary cache-hit return path (and the not-cached-yet resolution loop) returns unwrapped models from session.identityProviders().getById(id), so the same query returns organization-wrapped models on a cold cache and unwrapped models on a warm cache. The same login-page request produces different IDP model behavior depending on cache state: OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java line 75/80 explicitly adds 'idp.isEnabled() &&' with the comment 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped', proving the wrapper changes observable state — on a warm cache that re-check is a no-op and IDPs that the wrapper would have suppressed pass the filter, so the rendered broker list differs between a cold and warm Infinispan cache.

[ADVISORY] testCacheIDPForLogin never executes the cache-hit return path (query != null && cached != null) nor the chained-query branch (cached == null): every getForLogin call in the test happens in a run where the key was just invalidated or never populated, so the feature's core behavior — serving the login IDP list from cache — is never verified for correct results. A regression in the hit path (e.g., the missing organization-aware wrapping above, a wrong searchKey lookup returning the wrong org's IDP set, or getById resolution returning stale/incorrect models) passes this test green, because the test only asserts cache-entry existence and invalidation, never that a subsequent getForLogin on a warm cache returns the right IDPs.

[ADVISORY] The new getLoginPredicate clause requiring OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC for org-linked IDPs has no test coverage: every org-linked IDP created in testCacheIDPForLogin (i >= 10, and idp-alias-20 in step 4) sets BROKER_PUBLIC=TRUE, so no test ever exercises an org-linked IDP without BROKER_PUBLIC being excluded from getForLogin. This predicate change alters DB-level (non-cached) getForLogin results for every caller of getLoginPredicate, not just the cache; a regression that drops or mis-evaluates the new clause (e.g., making org-linked non-public brokers visible on the login page realm-wide) is undetectable by this test suite since all org-linked fixtures are public.

[BUG] The cleanup registration 'getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)' references alias "alias", but the IDPs created in the loop have aliases "idp-alias-0".."idp-alias-19", so none of the 20 created providers are ever cleaned up and the cleanup invokes remove on a nonexistent resource 20 times. The 20 identity providers leak past the test's cleanup (only the explicitly removed idp-alias-1 is deleted), and each of the 20 registered cleanups attempts to delete a non-existent 'alias' provider (404 on remove), polluting subsequent tests in the same realm and risking cleanup failures.

[ADVISORY] The remove() login-invalidation branch (registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) firing for a login-eligible IDP) is never exercised: the only removal in testCacheIDPForLogin is idp-alias-1, a disabled/non-login IDP, which asserts the caches survive. If remove() fails to invalidate the login caches for a login-eligible provider (e.g., the storedIdp fetch or predicate test regresses), a deleted broker keeps appearing on the login page until cache expiry; no test in this diff would catch it, since only the negative (no-invalidation) removal path is asserted.

[ADVISORY] Login-cache invalidation for organization-link changes exists only inside registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate (fired from update()), and the test covers only the add-link direction; there is no test that removing an IDP from an organization or deleting the organization clears the login caches. If the org provider's removeIdentityProvider or organization-deletion path mutates the link without routing through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update, the login caches go stale — a broker removed from an org keeps being served by getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL) for that org, and a broker whose link was removed keeps being excluded from REALM_ONLY — and the diff provides no invalidation hook or test that would detect either direction.

[BUG] The added `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))` clause in LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate is a functional change to getForLogin filtering for every IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementation (JPA, map store, any custom SPI impl), not just the Infinispan cache this PR claims to add. Deployments using a non-cached identity provider storage silently stop returning organization-linked IDPs that lack BROKER_PUBLIC from getForLogin (ORG_ONLY/ALL) after upgrade — IDPs disappear from org login pages with no cache involved; the change is not traceable to the stated 'add caching support' intent and should be split out or explicitly declared as a semantic change to the SPI contract.

[BUG] getForLogin returns createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel-wrapped models on the isInvalid/fallback return path but bare models from session.identityProviders().getById on the cache-hit and cache-fill paths, so the same method returns two different model contracts depending on cache state. Callers such as OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean receive org-aware wrapped models when the login query is invalid but bare cached adapters when it is cached, for identical inputs in the same realm — any consumer behavior that depends on the wrapper diverges between a cold and a warm cache, and the wrapping applied in the miss branches is discarded anyway (only getInternalId is consumed) except on the isInvalid path.

[ADVISORY] Correctness of the new login caches for organization-link changes rests entirely on the implicit invariant that every org link/unlink mutation flows through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update (so registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate sees the organizationId change); the diff adds no hook or assertion in the organization provider side and the new test covers only adding a link, never removing one. If any current or future org-provider path mutates the link without an IDP update call (e.g., a direct mapping-table write), all three login caches keep serving the stale IDP set cluster-wide until eviction, and users see brokers on login pages that are no longer linked (or miss newly linked ones); an unlink regression would ship with no test to catch it.

[ADVISORY] The cache-fill sequence (getCurrentRevision, delegate fetch mapping to internalIds, construct IdentityProviderListQuery, addRevisioned) is duplicated across the query==null and cached==null branches, and the copies have already drifted: the first seeds with startupRevision while the second uses cache.getCurrentCounter(). The next change to the fill logic must be applied in two places and an editor touching one branch will miss the other; the unexplained divergence in revision source is either a latent staleness bug or undocumented intent that gets copied forward into future cache implementations built on the same pattern.

[BUG] Inside the creation loop, cleanup registers `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove`, targeting an IDP alias 'alias' that this test never creates, instead of the just-created 'idp-alias-' + i alias. All 20 created IDPs are never removed by these cleanup registrations (each remove call targets a non-existent 'alias' resource), so the test leaks its IDPs into the shared TEST_REALM_NAME realm and subsequent tests in the class run against polluted identity-provider state.

[BUG] The cleanup for the newly created 'idp-alias-20' provider likewise registers `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` — the wrong alias, repeating the same copy-paste defect as the loop site. 'idp-alias-20', the very provider the later invalidation steps mutate, is never cleaned up, so it persists in the realm after the test and can alter getForLogin counts and login listings for subsequent tests in the class.

[BUG] A PR whose stated objective is 'add caching support for getForLogin' silently changes the shared login predicate semantics by adding the organization-public clause to getLoginPredicate(), altering results for every existing caller and for the uncached delegate path, not just the new cache. Any deployment with enabled, org-linked identity providers that do not carry OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC=true in their config stops having those IDPs returned by getForLogin after upgrade, so brokers that previously appeared on the login page disappear — a user-visible login-behavior change smuggled into a caching PR that was never stated as part of the objective.

[BUG] The warm-cache path of getForLogin returns raw models resolved via session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both cold paths (isInvalid and the idp==null fallback) wrap every result, so callers receive observably different model behavior depending on cache warmth. The author's own compensating change in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean (the added 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped' filter) proves wrapped and unwrapped models differ in observable state; any caller other than that bean — e.g. broker login flows consuming getForLogin directly — gets wrapped models on the first call after invalidation and unwrapped models on every subsequent cached call, yielding different enabled/organization behavior for the same request depending on whether the cache happens to be warm.

[ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) on every invocation, whereas the pre-diff code only hit the delegate when the cache key was already invalid. Every IDP removal — including the previously-served path where the cached CachedIdentityProvider already supplied the internalId for invalidation — now pays an extra database lookup on the delegate, adding a DB read to an admin operation that previously completed from cache in the common case.

[ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate makes its skip-invalidation decision by comparing the incoming update model against idpById obtained from the realm cache (getById), so a stale cached copy can make a genuine login-availability transition look like a no-transition. If this node's cached copy of the IDP is stale relative to the database (e.g. another node changed enabled/BROKER_PUBLIC and the invalidation hasn't been processed), an update that actually transitions the IDP in or out of login eligibility is classified as 'preserves that' and the login caches are not invalidated, leaving realms serving a stale set of login IDPs until some unrelated invalidation fires.

[BUG] The cleanup registration inside the creation loop calls testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, removing a nonexistent IDP named 'alias' instead of the just-created 'idp-alias-' + i providers. The twenty IDPs created by the test are never removed by this cleanup registration, so they leak into subsequent tests running in the same realm and can skew assertions (e.g. the exact-count assertEquals on login-cache sizes) in other OrganizationCacheTest or organization tests that run after this one.

[ADVISORY] Step 4 of the test conflates two operations — it sets BROKER_PUBLIC via an update() (which alone invalidates the login caches per the registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate logic under test) immediately before addIdentityProvider — so the assertion 'linking to an org invalidates the caches' is never actually isolated or verified. The riskiest invalidation assumption in the design — that all organization-link changes (addIdentityProvider, unlinking, and organization deletion) route through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update() and therefore trigger registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate — is untested; if any org-linkage path mutates the IDP's organizationId without invoking the cached provider's update(), login caches go stale with no invalidation and the test suite still passes, giving false confidence in the cache-coherence contract.

[BUG] getForLogin applies the organization-aware security wrapping (createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, which enforces org-scoped broker visibility via isEnabled) only on the isInvalid(cacheKey) path, while the warm-cache path resolves models via session.identityProviders().getById(id) and returns them unwrapped. The org-context visibility control over identity providers is enforced inconsistently depending on cache temperature: on a cache hit, callers receive raw cached models in which the wrapper's org-based isEnabled() suppression is absent, so any consumer of getForLogin that relies on the wrapped model to hide brokers linked to organizations outside the caller's context will instead serve them once the login list is warm. The diff itself acknowledges the divergence (OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java line ~75/81 adds a re-check 'idp.isEnabled() as idp might have been wrapped'), but only the patched bean is compensated; the cold-vs-warm behavioral split remains for every other call site and for the isInvalid-vs-cached paths of the same method.

[BUG] The cleanup registration inside the IDP-creation loop calls testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, but no IDP with alias "alias" is ever created — the created IDPs are "idp-alias-0" through "idp-alias-19". The 20 IDPs created by this test are never removed by cleanup (the registered remover targets a non-existent 'alias' provider, failing or no-oping on each of the 21 registrations), so realm state leaks into other tests in the suite and cleanup itself reports errors.

[BUG] The second cleanup registration for the newly created idp-alias-20 also references the non-existent alias "alias" (getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)). idp-alias-20 is never cleaned up after the test, leaving a leftover enabled identity provider in the test realm that can affect subsequent tests relying on realm state.

[ADVISORY] The new 'cache entry exists but this searchKey is not yet cached' branch in getForLogin (invalidateObject + chained IdentityProviderListQuery) is never exercised: I checked the only test file in the diff (OrganizationCacheTest.java) and it calls each FetchMode with exactly one organizationId (REALM_ONLY with null, ORG_ONLY with orgaId, ALL with orgaId), so query.getIDPs(searchKey) is never null on a hit. A regression in the chained-query construction (e.g., wrong revision counter, dropped chained keys) would merge or lose per-organization IDP sets for subsequent searches and no test in this diff would fail.

[ADVISORY] The true path of registerIDPLoginInvalidation reached from create() and remove() is never asserted: in OrganizationCacheTest.java the only create is a hideOnLogin (non-login) IDP and the only remove is idp-alias-1 (a disabled, non-login IDP), so 'create a login-qualified IDP invalidates the login caches' and 'remove a login-qualified IDP invalidates the login caches' are both untested. If the create/remove invalidation calls are dropped or the predicate mis-fires, newly created or removed brokers keep appearing/disappearing on the login page for up to the cache lifetime; no test in this diff would catch it.

[ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate is only tested in the unqualified→qualified direction (scenario 3 and 4); the reverse transition — updating a currently login-qualified IDP so it stops qualifying (e.g., disabling it or setting hideOnLogin) — is never exercised in OrganizationCacheTest.java. If the second early-return condition or the predicate comparison is wrong in that direction, a disabled broker remains listed on the login page from cache after an admin disables it, and no test in this diff detects it.

[ADVISORY] The new predicate disjunct (idp.getOrganizationId() == null || BROKER_PUBLIC) is only tested in its true forms: every org-linked IDP created in OrganizationCacheTest.java (i >= 10) has BROKER_PUBLIC=TRUE, so the case the clause exists to exclude — an org-linked IDP without BROKER_PUBLIC — is never created and never shown to be filtered out. A regression that drops the BROKER_PUBLIC check (making all org-linked IDPs login-eligible) leaves every assertion in testCacheIDPForLogin passing, so non-public organization brokers would silently appear on login pages.

[ADVISORY] The added idp.isEnabled() re-check in both filter branches of searchForIdentityProviders has no test: the only test file changed in this diff (OrganizationCacheTest.java) never touches OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean or any Freemarker login rendering path. If the re-check is removed or inverted (or the wrapped model is always enabled/always disabled), the login page's broker list changes and no test in this diff fails; the comment-justified behavior ('idp might have been wrapped') is verified by nothing.

[ADVISORY] The test asserts only internal cache structure (IdentityProviderListQuery presence and getIDPs(...) set sizes via realmCache.getCache()) and discards every getForLogin return value, so it never verifies the actual IdentityProviderModels the cached path returns. A cached-path regression that returns wrong, stale, or non-organization-aware models (the reason OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean needed the isEnabled re-check in this very diff) passes all assertions, because the set of internal IDs matches even when the resolved models are wrong.

[BUG] The new predicate term `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))` makes BROKER_PUBLIC-absent evaluate to false (Boolean.parseBoolean(null) == false), silently reclassifying every existing organization-linked identity provider as not-available-for-login, and the diff ships no data migration or backfill to populate BROKER_PUBLIC on pre-existing org-linked IDPs. On upgrade, every realm with org-linked IDPs that never had OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC set in their config loses those brokers from getForLogin results in ALL fetch modes — including the org-specific fetch (ALL, organizationId) in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders, where previously any enabled linked IDP was offered to the org's members. Users of those orgs silently stop seeing their brokers on the login page with no error and no admin-facing signal; fixing it requires an operator to hand-edit each IDP's config because there is no migration/backfill step setting BROKER_PUBLIC=true for already-linked IDPs.

[BUG] getForLogin returns different model objects depending on cache warmth: the isInvalid path (line 218) and the idp==null fallback (line 248) wrap results with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while the cache-populate path and the cache-hit path return unwrapped models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) (lines 249-254), so identical data yields org-aware-wrapped models on a cold/invalidated cache and raw models on a warm cache. Callers get silently different behavior for the same underlying data depending on whether the cache was warm: the caller in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean explicitly compensates with an isEnabled() re-check 'as idp might have been wrapped' (services/.../OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java lines 75 and 80), which filters IDPs differently for wrapped vs raw models — so the same login request can render a different set of login IDPs before and after a cache invalidation, and any consumer that relies on the org-aware wrapping (org-scoped broker resolution) loses that context entirely on cache hits.

[ADVISORY] Every getForLogin call with an organizationId whose searchKey is not yet cached under the per-mode key executes cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey), evicting the single shared per-realm-per-mode login list entry (and its cluster-wide invalidation) just to add one more searchKey. On a login hot path in an org-heavy realm, each first login under a new organization id drops the whole per-mode login cache across all cluster nodes, forcing every node to re-query the database for every previously cached searchKey of that mode; with N organizations this is a recurring cluster-wide cache flush and DB spike triggered by ordinary user logins, invisible to operators as an error because the requests all still succeed.

[ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally executes idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) before any cache check, adding a database read to every remove call where previously the delegate was consulted only when the cache entry was invalid. Every IDP removal — including no-op removals of nonexistent aliases, where storedIdp is null, no invalidation is needed, and remove returns false — pays an extra database roundtrip on the admin path; the pre-existing cached CachedIdentityProvider entry in the else branch (lines 103-106) is now redundant with the delegate lookup, leaving two sources consulted where one sufficed.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `getForLogin` implementation, the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` path and the `idp == null` fallback both return `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, explicitly wrapping results. From the diff alone, that means cold-cache vs warm-cache can return different `IdentityProviderModel` instances (wrapped vs not wrapped) for the same `getForLogin` call, which is an observable behavioral inconsistency and a correctness defect risk.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, every `getForLogin(...)` invocation that occurs in the test is either the first time for that `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` (so `query == null` branch in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`), or it happens after the test asserts caches were cleared and then re-populates them again (still `query == null`). The later `RunOnServer` blocks only assert cache entry presence/absence and do not call `getForLogin` again on a warm cache. As a result, the cache-hit path (`query != null` and `cached != null`) and the chained-query path (`cached == null` for a new `searchKey` on an existing query) are never exercised/validated for correct returned IDPs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new login-eligibility condition in `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` requiring org-linked IDPs to have `OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC` set true (`idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(...))`). In `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`, every IDP later linked to an org (loop `i >= 10` and `idp-alias-20` in step 4) explicitly sets `BROKER_PUBLIC` to `TRUE`, and no fixture creates an org-linked IDP with `BROKER_PUBLIC` absent/false to assert it is excluded from `getForLogin`. So the new predicate branch is not exercised by tests, and regressions in that clause would not be caught.

In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, the only removal is `idp-alias-1`, which was created with `setEnabled((i % 2) == 0)` so it is disabled and thus not login-eligible, and the test asserts caches remain. adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new getForLogin() cache keyed by realm+FetchMode and invalidates it on IDP create/update/remove via registerIDPLoginInvalidation*(). The new test (testCacheIDPForLogin) exercises cache population and invalidation on IDP update (hideOnLogin flip) and on adding an org link (step 4), but it does not cover the reverse direction (removing an IDP from an org) or organization deletion. The finding’s claim that org-link removal/deletion might bypass IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update() and thus leave the login cache stale cannot be verified from this diff because the org provider/link-removal code path is not shown. However, the absence of tests for those directions is a concrete, diff-grounded gap given the new cache behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The added `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))` clause in LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate is a functional change to getForLogin filtering for every IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementation (JPA, map store, any custom SPI impl), not just the Infinispan cache this PR claims to add. Deployments using a non-cached identity provider storage silently stop returning organization-linked IDPs that lack BROKER_PUBLIC from getForLogin (ORG_ONLY/ALL) after upgrade — IDPs disappear from org login pages with no cache involved; the change is not traceable to the stated 'add caching support' intent and should be split out or explicitly declared as a semantic change to the SPI contract.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. Since this method is in the SPI (`server-spi`) and not Infinispan-specific, it is a behavioral/contract change that can affect any codepath/implementation that relies on `getLoginPredicate()` for `getForLogin`-style filtering, beyond the new Infinispan caching logic. The diff itself doesn’t prove this is incorrect behavior, but it does show the PR is not purely “add caching support” and introduces a cross-implementation semantic constraint on org-linked IDPs unless `BROKER_PUBLIC` is true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getForLogin returns createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel-wrapped models on the isInvalid/fallback return path but bare models from session.identityProviders().getById on the cache-hit and cache-fill paths, so the same method returns two different model contracts depending on cache state. Callers such as OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean receive org-aware wrapped models when the login query is invalid but bare cached adapters when it is cached, for identical inputs in the same realm — any consumer behavior that depends on the wrapper diverges between a cold and a warm cache, and the wrapping applied in the miss branches is discarded anyway (only getInternalId is consumed) except on the isInvalid path.

adjudication.rationale: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin, the isInvalid(cacheKey) path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the normal cached/cache-fill path builds a `Set<String>` of internalIds and then returns `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` results directly (`return identityProviders.stream();`) without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. From the diff alone, this makes the method return differently wrapped IdentityProviderModel instances depending on cache state for the same inputs, matching the finding’s inconsistency concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Correctness of the new login caches for organization-link changes rests entirely on the implicit invariant that every org link/unlink mutation flows through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update (so registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate sees the organizationId change); the diff adds no hook or assertion in the organization provider side and the new test covers only adding a link, never removing one. If any current or future org-provider path mutates the link without an IDP update call (e.g., a direct mapping-table write), all three login caches keep serving the stale IDP set cluster-wide until eviction, and users see brokers on login pages that are no longer linked (or miss newly linked ones); an unlink regression would ship with no test to catch it.

adjudication.rationale: The new login-result caching is keyed only by realm+FetchMode (cacheKeyForLogin) but stores per-organization result sets inside IdentityProviderListQuery. InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider invalidates these caches only from IDP create/update/remove paths (registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate / remove), and nothing in this diff shows any invalidation hook on the organization-link mutation side. The added test (testCacheIDPForLogin) exercises linking an IDP to an org (step 4) but does not cover unlink/removal of the org link. While the diff doesn’t prove an actual bug (the org-link API might call update internally), it does introduce a nontrivial correctness dependency and leaves a key edge-case (unlink) untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cache-fill sequence (getCurrentRevision, delegate fetch mapping to internalIds, construct IdentityProviderListQuery, addRevisioned) is duplicated across the query==null and cached==null branches, and the copies have already drifted: the first seeds with startupRevision while the second uses cache.getCurrentCounter(). The next change to the fill logic must be applied in two places and an editor touching one branch will miss the other; the unexplained divergence in revision source is either a latent staleness bug or undocumented intent that gets copied forward into future cache implementations built on the same pattern.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added getForLogin() caching logic, the cache-fill sequence is indeed duplicated in two branches: (1) when query == null it does `Long loaded = cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey); ... query = new IdentityProviderListQuery(...); cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision);`, and (2) when `cached == null` it repeats the same sequence but ends with `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter());`. This drift (startupRevision vs currentCounter) is directly visible in the diff and creates a concrete maintainability risk and a potentially confusing/incorrect inconsistency, but the diff alone does not prove it causes incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Inside the creation loop, cleanup registers `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove`, targeting an IDP alias 'alias' that this test never creates, instead of the just-created 'idp-alias-' + i alias. All 20 created IDPs are never removed by these cleanup registrations (each remove call targets a non-existent 'alias' resource), so the test leaks its IDPs into the shared TEST_REALM_NAME realm and subsequent tests in the class run against polluted identity-provider state.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin()`, the loop creates IDPs with aliases `"idp-alias-" + i`, but the cleanup registration uses `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);`, which targets a literal alias "alias" that is not created in this test. As a result, the per-iteration cleanup will not remove the newly created IDPs, potentially leaking them into the realm state for subsequent tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup for the newly created 'idp-alias-20' provider likewise registers `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` — the wrong alias, repeating the same copy-paste defect as the loop site. 'idp-alias-20', the very provider the later invalidation steps mutate, is never cleaned up, so it persists in the realm after the test and can alter getForLogin counts and login listings for subsequent tests in the class.

This means the new providers are not cleaned up by this test, so they can persist and affect subsequent tests' login IDP counts/listings as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] A PR whose stated objective is 'add caching support for getForLogin' silently changes the shared login predicate semantics by adding the organization-public clause to getLoginPredicate(), altering results for every existing caller and for the uncached delegate path, not just the new cache. Any deployment with enabled, org-linked identity providers that do not carry OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC=true in their config stops having those IDPs returned by getForLogin after upgrade, so brokers that previously appeared on the login page disappear — a user-visible login-behavior change smuggled into a caching PR that was never stated as part of the objective.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change shared semantics: `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` now adds `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`, which will exclude org-linked IDPs unless `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` (server-spi change). This affects all current and future callers of `getLoginPredicate()` (including uncached delegate paths), not just the new Infinispan caching. However, from the diff alone we cannot verify that this is incorrect behavior vs an intended functional change, so it’s best classified as a scope/behavior-change review concern rather than a provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The warm-cache path of getForLogin returns raw models resolved via session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both cold paths (isInvalid and the idp==null fallback) wrap every result, so callers receive observably different model behavior depending on cache warmth. The author's own compensating change in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean (the added 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped' filter) proves wrapped and unwrapped models differ in observable state; any caller other than that bean — e.g. broker login flows consuming getForLogin directly — gets wrapped models on the first call after invalidation and unwrapped models on every subsequent cached call, yielding different enabled/organization behavior for the same request depending on whether the cache happens to be warm.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, both cold paths wrap results with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (`isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch and the `idp == null` fallback), but the warm-cache path resolves IDs via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying the wrapper. This makes returned model behavior depend on whether the cache is warm. The accompanying change in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` explicitly notes “idp might have been wrapped” and adds an `idp.isEnabled()` re-check, reinforcing that wrapped vs unwrapped models are observably different; other callers would still see inconsistent behavior across warm/cold cache paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) on every invocation, whereas the pre-diff code only hit the delegate when the cache key was already invalid. Every IDP removal — including the previously-served path where the cached CachedIdentityProvider already supplied the internalId for invalidation — now pays an extra database lookup on the delegate, adding a DB read to an admin operation that previously completed from cache in the common case.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `remove(String alias)` now does `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)`, so it always hits the delegate even when the cache is valid and the `CachedIdentityProvider` could supply the internalId (the pre-diff behavior only called the delegate in the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch). This adds an unconditional delegate lookup (likely DB read) to the previously cached path, which is a concrete performance/efficiency regression, not a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate makes its skip-invalidation decision by comparing the incoming update model against idpById obtained from the realm cache (getById), so a stale cached copy can make a genuine login-availability transition look like a no-transition. If this node's cached copy of the IDP is stale relative to the database (e.g. another node changed enabled/BROKER_PUBLIC and the invalidation hasn't been processed), an update that actually transitions the IDP in or out of login eligibility is classified as 'preserves that' and the login caches are not invalidated, leaving realms serving a stale set of login IDPs until some unrelated invalidation fires.

adjudication.rationale: In update(), the “original” model used by registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated) is obtained via getById(model.getInternalId()). In this Infinispan cache-backed provider, getById is expected to consult the local realm cache (not shown in this diff), so the skip-invalidations checks (both not-login, or both login + same organizationId) can be made against a potentially stale local copy. If the local cached ‘original’ incorrectly matches the ‘updated’ login-eligibility state, the method returns early and does not invalidate the new login-list caches (cacheKeyForLogin(...)), allowing stale login IDP sets to persist. This risk is directly tied to the new early-return logic added in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup registration inside the creation loop calls testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, removing a nonexistent IDP named 'alias' instead of the just-created 'idp-alias-' + i providers. The twenty IDPs created by the test are never removed by this cleanup registration, so they leak into subsequent tests running in the same realm and can skew assertions (e.g. the exact-count assertEquals on login-cache sizes) in other OrganizationCacheTest or organization tests that run after this one.

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `testCacheIDPForLogin`, inside the creation loop the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` instead of targeting the just-created provider (`"idp-alias-" + i`). This would attempt to remove a (likely) nonexistent IDP named `alias`, leaving the 20 created IDPs in place and potentially polluting subsequent tests in the same realm, which can affect later count-based assertions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Step 4 of the test conflates two operations — it sets BROKER_PUBLIC via an update() (which alone invalidates the login caches per the registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate logic under test) immediately before addIdentityProvider — so the assertion 'linking to an org invalidates the caches' is never actually isolated or verified. The riskiest invalidation assumption in the design — that all organization-link changes (addIdentityProvider, unlinking, and organization deletion) route through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update() and therefore trigger registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate — is untested; if any org-linkage path mutates the IDP's organizationId without invoking the cached provider's update(), login caches go stale with no invalidation and the test suite still passes, giving false confidence in the cache-coherence contract.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that in test step 4 the preceding IdentityProvider update() “alone invalidates the login caches per the registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate logic”. But the added logic in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate explicitly *does not* invalidate when both original and updated qualify for login and the organizationId is unchanged (Objects.equals(original.getOrganizationId(), updated.getOrganizationId())). In step 4, the update() only sets BROKER_PUBLIC while the IDP’s organizationId is still null (the org link is added after), and the login predicate is already satisfied when organizationId is null, so the update path would return early and not invalidate login caches. The broader concern about org-linkage mutations bypassing IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update() is speculative and cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getForLogin applies the organization-aware security wrapping (createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, which enforces org-scoped broker visibility via isEnabled) only on the isInvalid(cacheKey) path, while the warm-cache path resolves models via session.identityProviders().getById(id) and returns them unwrapped. The org-context visibility control over identity providers is enforced inconsistently depending on cache temperature: on a cache hit, callers receive raw cached models in which the wrapper's org-based isEnabled() suppression is absent, so any consumer of getForLogin that relies on the wrapped model to hide brokers linked to organizations outside the caller's context will instead serve them once the login list is warm. The diff itself acknowledges the divergence (OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java line ~75/81 adds a re-check 'idp.isEnabled() as idp might have been wrapped'), but only the patched bean is compensated; the cold-vs-warm behavioral split remains for every other call site and for the isInvalid-vs-cached paths of the same method.

adjudication.rationale: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin, the cache-miss/invalid path explicitly wraps results with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel (`return idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel);`), but the warm-cache path reconstructs results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns them without applying that wrapper. This creates a verifiable cold-vs-warm behavioral divergence in the same method, consistent with the compensating change in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean (re-checking `idp.isEnabled()` because it “might have been wrapped”). Any org-aware visibility/enabled suppression implemented by the wrapper will not be enforced on cache hits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup registration inside the IDP-creation loop calls testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, but no IDP with alias "alias" is ever created — the created IDPs are "idp-alias-0" through "idp-alias-19". The 20 IDPs created by this test are never removed by cleanup (the registered remover targets a non-existent 'alias' provider, failing or no-oping on each of the 21 registrations), so realm state leaks into other tests in the suite and cleanup itself reports errors.

adjudication.rationale: In OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin(), the loop creates IDPs with aliases "idp-alias-0" through "idp-alias-19", but registers cleanup with testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove each time. The diff shows no IDP with alias "alias" is created, so the registered cleanup targets the wrong resource and will not remove the created IDPs, causing test state leakage and/or cleanup errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The second cleanup registration for the newly created idp-alias-20 also references the non-existent alias "alias" (getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)). idp-alias-20 is never cleaned up after the test, leaving a leftover enabled identity provider in the test realm that can affect subsequent tests relying on realm state.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, after creating IDPs the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (appears in the 0..19 loop and again after creating `idp-alias-20`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new 'cache entry exists but this searchKey is not yet cached' branch in getForLogin (invalidateObject + chained IdentityProviderListQuery) is never exercised: I checked the only test file in the diff (OrganizationCacheTest.java) and it calls each FetchMode with exactly one organizationId (REALM_ONLY with null, ORG_ONLY with orgaId, ALL with orgaId), so query.getIDPs(searchKey) is never null on a hit. A regression in the chained-query construction (e.g., wrong revision counter, dropped chained keys) would merge or lose per-organization IDP sets for subsequent searches and no test in this diff would fail.

adjudication.rationale: In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the new branch `if (cached == null) { ... invalidateObject(cacheKey); ... query = new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query); }` is only taken when a cache entry for `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` exists but does not yet contain the specific `searchKey` (derived from `organizationId`). In `OrganizationCacheTest#testCacheIDPForLogin`, each `FetchMode` is exercised with only one `organizationId` value (`REALM_ONLY` with null/"", `ORG_ONLY` with `orgaId`, `ALL` with `orgaId`), so once the query is cached, subsequent reads use the same `searchKey` and will not make `query.getIDPs(searchKey)` return null. Therefore the diff’s added chained-query behavior for multiple `organizationId` values per mode is not covered by the new test, making the finding (missing coverage for that nontrivial branch) accurate and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The true path of registerIDPLoginInvalidation reached from create() and remove() is never asserted: in OrganizationCacheTest.java the only create is a hideOnLogin (non-login) IDP and the only remove is idp-alias-1 (a disabled, non-login IDP), so 'create a login-qualified IDP invalidates the login caches' and 'remove a login-qualified IDP invalidates the login caches' are both untested. If the create/remove invalidation calls are dropped or the predicate mis-fires, newly created or removed brokers keep appearing/disappearing on the login page for up to the cache lifetime; no test in this diff would catch it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new login-cache invalidation paths in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.create()` and `remove()` via `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(...)`, which only triggers when `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` is true. In `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin()`, the only created IDP (`idp-alias-20`) is explicitly `hideOnLogin=true` (intended to be unavailable for login), and the only removal is `idp-alias-1`, which was created with `enabled=false` (odd index), so it also won’t qualify for login. The test asserts caches are *not* invalidated in those scenarios, but it never asserts that creating/removing a login-qualified IDP *does* invalidate the login caches. That’s a specific, diff-grounded coverage gap for newly added behavior, not a demonstrated functional defect in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate is only tested in the unqualified→qualified direction (scenario 3 and 4); the reverse transition — updating a currently login-qualified IDP so it stops qualifying (e.g., disabling it or setting hideOnLogin) — is never exercised in OrganizationCacheTest.java. If the second early-return condition or the predicate comparison is wrong in that direction, a disabled broker remains listed on the login page from cache after an admin disables it, and no test in this diff detects it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial conditional invalidation logic in `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(...)` (early returns based on `getLoginPredicate()` and `Objects.equals(original.getOrganizationId(), updated.getOrganizationId())`). The new `OrganizationCacheTest#testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises cache invalidation when an IDP becomes login-eligible (scenario 3: `hideOnLogin` true→false; scenario 4 also asserts invalidation after changes), but it does not exercise the opposite transition where a previously login-qualified IDP becomes unqualified (e.g., `setEnabled(false)` or `setHideOnLogin(true)`). That is a specific, diff-grounded test gap for the newly added invalidation paths, not a proven defect in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new predicate disjunct (idp.getOrganizationId() == null || BROKER_PUBLIC) is only tested in its true forms: every org-linked IDP created in OrganizationCacheTest.java (i >= 10) has BROKER_PUBLIC=TRUE, so the case the clause exists to exclude — an org-linked IDP without BROKER_PUBLIC — is never created and never shown to be filtered out. A regression that drops the BROKER_PUBLIC check (making all org-linked IDPs login-eligible) leaves every assertion in testCacheIDPForLogin passing, so non-public organization brokers would silently appear on login pages.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds a new eligibility condition in `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()`:
```java
.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))
```
However, the new test `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin()` only creates org-linked IDPs (i >= 10) with `BROKER_PUBLIC` explicitly set to `TRUE`, and does not create any org-linked IDP with `BROKER_PUBLIC` missing/false to prove it is excluded from `getForLogin(...)`. Therefore, the new predicate branch meant to filter out non-public org brokers is not negatively tested; removing the `BROKER_PUBLIC` check would not change any of the asserted counts in this test because no such non-public org-linked IDP exists in the setup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The added idp.isEnabled() re-check in both filter branches of searchForIdentityProviders has no test: the only test file changed in this diff (OrganizationCacheTest.java) never touches OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean or any Freemarker login rendering path. If the re-check is removed or inverted (or the wrapped model is always enabled/always disabled), the login page's broker list changes and no test in this diff fails; the comment-justified behavior ('idp might have been wrapped') is verified by nothing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders by adding `idp.isEnabled()` to both filter branches (lines changed in that file). The only added/modified test in this diff is `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`, which exercises `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` and cache invalidation, but never touches `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` or any Freemarker/login rendering path. Therefore, removing/inverting the new `isEnabled()` re-check (or changing wrapper behavior) would not be caught by tests in this diff. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The test asserts only internal cache structure (IdentityProviderListQuery presence and getIDPs(...) set sizes via realmCache.getCache()) and discards every getForLogin return value, so it never verifies the actual IdentityProviderModels the cached path returns. A cached-path regression that returns wrong, stale, or non-organization-aware models (the reason OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean needed the isEnabled re-check in this very diff) passes all assertions, because the set of internal IDs matches even when the resolved models are wrong.

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `testCacheIDPForLogin`, the calls to `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` discard the returned `Stream<IdentityProviderModel>` and never assert anything about the resulting models. All assertions instead inspect internal cache state via `realmCache.getCache().get(cacheKeyForLogin(...), IdentityProviderListQuery.class)` and only check presence and `getIDPs(searchKey).size()`. This means the test would still pass if the cached-path resolution (e.g., `for (String id : cached) { session.identityProviders().getById(id) ... }`) returned wrong/stale/non-org-aware/wrapped models as long as the cached internal-id set sizes match. The diff even hints at model/wrapping nuances by adding `idp.isEnabled()` re-checks in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`, which this test does not validate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new predicate term `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))` makes BROKER_PUBLIC-absent evaluate to false (Boolean.parseBoolean(null) == false), silently reclassifying every existing organization-linked identity provider as not-available-for-login, and the diff ships no data migration or backfill to populate BROKER_PUBLIC on pre-existing org-linked IDPs. On upgrade, every realm with org-linked IDPs that never had OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC set in their config loses those brokers from getForLogin results in ALL fetch modes — including the org-specific fetch (ALL, organizationId) in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders, where previously any enabled linked IDP was offered to the org's members. Users of those orgs silently stop seeing their brokers on the login page with no error and no admin-facing signal; fixing it requires an operator to hand-edit each IDP's config because there is no migration/backfill step setting BROKER_PUBLIC=true for already-linked IDPs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() to require `BROKER_PUBLIC` for any IDP with a non-null `organizationId` (`idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`). Since `idp.getConfig().get(...)` can be null, `Boolean.parseBoolean(null)` is false, so org-linked IDPs lacking that config key will now fail the login predicate and be excluded from `getForLogin(...)` results (used by OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean). The PR adds no migration/backfill or automatic setting in the shown changes, so pre-existing org-linked IDPs without this config would silently disappear from login listings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getForLogin returns different model objects depending on cache warmth: the isInvalid path (line 218) and the idp==null fallback (line 248) wrap results with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while the cache-populate path and the cache-hit path return unwrapped models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) (lines 249-254), so identical data yields org-aware-wrapped models on a cold/invalidated cache and raw models on a warm cache. Callers get silently different behavior for the same underlying data depending on whether the cache was warm: the caller in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean explicitly compensates with an isEnabled() re-check 'as idp might have been wrapped' (services/.../OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java lines 75 and 80), which filters IDPs differently for wrapped vs raw models — so the same login request can render a different set of login IDPs before and after a cache invalidation, and any consumer that relies on the org-aware wrapping (org-scoped broker resolution) loses that context entirely on cache hits.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `getForLogin` implementation, the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)` (wrapped models). The `idp == null` fallback also returns wrapped models the same way. But on the normal cache-populate/cache-hit path, it collects internal IDs and then returns `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` results directly (`return identityProviders.stream();`) without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. From the diff alone, this means callers can receive different `IdentityProviderModel` instances/behavior depending on cache warmth. The change in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` adding an `isEnabled()` re-check explicitly acknowledges wrapper-dependent behavior, reinforcing that inconsistent wrapping can change observable filtering/output.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every getForLogin call with an organizationId whose searchKey is not yet cached under the per-mode key executes cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey), evicting the single shared per-realm-per-mode login list entry (and its cluster-wide invalidation) just to add one more searchKey. On a login hot path in an org-heavy realm, each first login under a new organization id drops the whole per-mode login cache across all cluster nodes, forcing every node to re-query the database for every previously cached searchKey of that mode; with N organizations this is a recurring cluster-wide cache flush and DB spike triggered by ordinary user logins, invisible to operators as an error because the requests all still succeed.

adjudication.rationale: In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin`, the cache key is only `realmId + ".idp.login." + fetchMode` (no organization/searchKey in the key). When a cached `IdentityProviderListQuery` exists but does not yet contain the current `searchKey` (`cached == null`), the code explicitly calls `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` before rebuilding and re-adding a new `IdentityProviderListQuery` that includes the additional searchKey (`new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)`). This means the single per-realm-per-mode entry is evicted whenever a previously unseen organizationId/searchKey is requested, which can cause avoidable cache churn on a login path. The performance/cluster-wide impact is plausible given typical Infinispan invalidation semantics, but the diff alone mainly verifies the per-mode entry eviction behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally executes idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) before any cache check, adding a database read to every remove call where previously the delegate was consulted only when the cache entry was invalid. Every IDP removal — including no-op removals of nonexistent aliases, where storedIdp is null, no invalidation is needed, and remove returns false — pays an extra database roundtrip on the admin path; the pre-existing cached CachedIdentityProvider entry in the else branch (lines 103-106) is now redundant with the delegate lookup, leaving two sources consulted where one sufficed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `remove(String alias)` now does `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` unconditionally before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. Previously, the delegate lookup only happened in the invalid-cache branch. With the new code, even when the cache entry is valid and `CachedIdentityProvider` could supply the internalId (else branch), the delegate lookup is still performed, effectively consulting two sources where one sufficed and adding an extra provider/DB read on every remove call. This is a concrete performance/regression concern, not a correctness defect visible from the diff.
